       CE Stephens Properties, LLC [Party 642] hereby files its Post Hearing Reply Brief, and

in support thereof shows as follows:

I.     INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY

       CE Stephens Properties, LLC (CE Stephens or Party 642) again expresses its sincere thanks

for the Administrative Law Judges’ (ALJs) attention to this case, their attention to the parties’

arguments, testimonies, and briefing.

       Your Honors now have the benefit of the parties’ post-hearing briefs, and though many

advocated either for specifically identified routes or generally against routes that used certain links,

no new record evidence was brought forth that should persuade Your Honors from finding that

Route 894 is the route that best meets the Commission’s routing criteria. A preponderance of the

evidence drives a finding that Route 894 best meets the Commission’s routing factors.

       The record evidence demonstrates that Route 894 performs well in historically important

routing factors, such as habitable structures, cost, length, paralleling, and environmental integrity,

other route may perform better on a particular routing factor; nevertheless, the Commission is

tasked with selecting the route that best overall meets the Commission’s routing criteria while also

satisfying the Commission’s policy goal of Prudent Avoidance.

        For instance, the Staff (Staff) of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission)

recommended route, Route 487, has better paralleling that Route 894, costs 0.77% less, and is

0.75% shorter; crucially however, these are immaterial advantages and come at a cost that is not

justified. 1 Route 487 impacts 11 more (12.9%) habitable structures, crosses nearly 9 miles (21%)

more of riparian area, and comes within a 100 feet of Colorado Bend State Park. 2

        Route 296, advocated for by intervenors such as the G9 and G13 Landowners and Save the

Lampasas, may have slightly better paralleling 3 and crosses a marginally shorter length (5,539 feet

Route 296 has over Route 894 in two routing factors are substantially outweighed by the fact that

296 costs about $3.64 million more than Route 894, and is 3,250 feet longer than Route 894. 6

        Route 572, advocated for by parties such as Save the Lampasas and the Link N3 Opposition

Landowners, impacts 13,694 fewer feet of riparian areas, but crucially, the advantages stop there. 7

VI.        ROUTE

           A.        Route 894 best meets the requirements of PURA and PUC substantive
                     rules.

           CE Stephens respectfully urges Your Honors to recommend the Commission adopt the

alternative route the Applicants identified as the route that best meets the Commission’s routing

criteria, Route 894. 11 Not only does Route 894 enjoy significant support from other intervenors,

but most importantly a preponderance of the record evidence demonstrates that Route 894 best

overall balances the routing factors set forth in 16 TAC § 25.101 and best satisfies the policy

objective of Prudent Avoidance.

           B.        Reply to Commission Staff’s Initial Brief

           CE Stephens urges Your Honors to reject Staff’s recommendation that the Commission

approve Route 487. Staff points to no record evidence to substantiate selecting Route 487 as the

route that best meets the Commission’s routing factors.

           Staff’s assertion that “Route 487 best balances the relevant criteria and is therefore the best

route option” and that “Route 487 exhibits reasonable quantitative criteria, while also exhibiting

qualitative features consistent with the community values expressed by parties and residents,” 12

finds no support in the credible evidence.

                     1.           Route 487’s Quantitative Features Are Without Merit

          Regarding Staff’s assertion that Route 487 “exhibits positive quantitative features,” and

the “quantitative criteria that most favor Route 487,” in fact do not demonstrate Route 487 to be

superior to Route 894. 13 Crucially, two of the four “quantitative features” Staff identifies to

substantiate Route 487 as the best meets route are equally true of Route 894. Route 894 also

crosses no upland woodlands and Route 894 also does not use Link E6. 14

          In regards to the first two quantitative criteria Staff points to that “most favor Route 487,”

paralleling and costs, Route 487’s stronger paralleling and marginal cost savings over Route 894

are outweighed by Route 894 impacting 12.9% fewer habitable structures 15 and crossing nearly

21% less riparian areas than Route 487; 16 and Route 487’s Link J11 comes within 100 feet of

Colorado Bend State Park. 17 Accordingly, CE Stephens urges Your Honors to afford no weight

to the quantitative features Staff provides in support of Route 487.

                    2.           Route 487’s Qualitative Features Lack Support in the Record
                                 Evidence

          CE Stephens urges Your Honors to afford no weight to Staff’s argument that Route 487

“performs well with regard to ‘community values’—a broadly construed term that is ‘properly

interpreted as a shared appreciation of an area or other natural or human resource by members of

a national, regional, or local community.’” 18 The selection of Route 487 would not and does not

satisfy Staff’s definition of community values.

           First, Staff cites the feedback provided by landowners at the three public meetings held by

the Applicants in Salado, Lampasas, and Menard, as a factor supportive of Route 487. 19 But Staff’s

recommended route, Route 487, does not mitigate the concerns raised by landowners at the three

public meetings held by the Applicants. 20

          Staff witness, Mr. Poole, cites comments from landowners regarding the transmission lines

proximity to residences, noting, for example, that “line H4 is very, very close to my house” and

“A2 route is running through my property.” 21          Mr. Poole goes on to cite comments from

landowners regarding aesthetics, such as “we purchased our land mostly for the view and your G2

line will ruin that.” 22 In Mr. Poole’s discussion of landowner comments regarding property values,

Mr. Poole cites comments from landowners who commented that “G4 power line will reduce the

property value by at least 50%.” 23 Mr. Poole also cited comments regarding environmental

concerns, for example that “the G5 link would also pass close to the Lampasas [R]iver and could

potentially cause issues with the unique river ecosystem.” 24

          Confusingly, in defending Route 487, Mr. Poole cites the fact that because Route 487 does

not use the specific links raised by landowners, such as Link H4, Route 487 somehow mitigates

the concerns expressed by members of the community and therefore satisfies the Commission’s

community values routing criteria. 25 Staff’s reliance on these landowner comments are misplaced

and fall short of lending support to Route 487 as a route that appeases concerns raised by the

community.

          While specifically addressing the “Community Values” routing criteria, Staff’s initial brief

asserts that “Route 487 ranks 16th in its utilization of existing transmission lines. Route 487 only

crosses 5.33% more ranchland pasture than the route that crosses the least amount of ranchland

pasture. Route 487 also parallels or utilizes compatible rights-of-way for nearly half of its total

length, which is the 4th most of any proposed alternative route. Notably, Route 487 does not utilize

several segments that received significant public opposition, such as Segments H41, H42, G1,

G42, G43, and G44, while also not utilizing Segment E6, which has the most habitable structures

within 500 feet of its centerline.” 26

         But as CE Stephens has already pointed out, Route 487’s stronger paralleling and slightly

lesser impact on rangeland pasture is vastly outweighed by the greater number of habitable

structures and riparian areas that it effects. 27 Furthermore, the fact that Route 487 does not use

Segments H41, H42, G1, G42, G43, and G44 is of no consequence, as a route must be evaluated

as a whole and not on whether it includes or excludes a specific link—a fact that Mr. Poole himself

concedes. 28

         Therefore, CE Stephens urges Your Honors to find that these statistics do nothing to

demonstrate how Route 487 is, overall, the route that best meets the Commission’s routing criteria,

or even the route that best meets the Commission’s community-values criteria, for that matter.

         A link cannot be evaluated in isolation. Rather, a route must be viewed as a whole and

how, as a whole, it balances the Commission’s routing criteria. 29 In fact during his deposition and

during the Hearing, Mr. Poole could not explain why a certain link, such as H4, was or was not

Furthermore, Route 487’s paralleling also results in fragmentation of properties, such as Sola Fe

fragmentation of properties that when grouped together form one contiguous property owned by

                    7.        Route 894 Best Achieves the Commission’s Policy Goal of Prudent
                              Avoidance

          Staff asserts that “20 of the 22 proposed alternative routes with less habitable structures are

more expensive, longer, and utilize less of their percentage length parallel to existing compatible

right-of-way and apparent property boundaries than Route 487.” 44 CE Stephens urges Your

Honors to afford no weight to this assertion.

          As CE Stephens has pointed out, Route 487 is only 0.75% shorter and 0.77% less expensive

than Route 894, and while Route 487 does have slightly better paralleling than Route 894, the vast

majority of Route 487 parallels apparent property boundaries rather than infrastructure such as

transmission line corridors or roads/highways. 45 Crucially, Staff’s comparison of Route 487 with

other routes does not paint a complete picture because Staff fails to point out that Route 487 also

crosses almost 47,000 more feet of riparian areas than Route 894, Route 487 comes within 100

Landowners, Carpenter Land & Cattle Company, and G9/G13 Landowners’ recommendation to

but when compared to all other alternative routes.

intervening landowner’s property. Not wanting a specific link to cross your property is not in and

landowner wants a transmission line to run across, or even adjacent to, their property. And Route
